title: Quantile-slice benchmarking vignette: throughput vs cost across session shapes
content:
Purpose:
This vignette captures a small, repeatable benchmark that slices latency by request quantiles (p50/p90/p95/p99) across session shapes (prompt+gen length distributions), model variants, and runtime knobs. Goal is to produce lightweight collateral that product, SRE, and solutions teams can use to set expectations and pick default policies for canary and Dedicated configs.

Key takeaways (top-level):
- p50 is a weak proxy for user experience when workload has heavy tails (chat sessions with occasional long generations). p95 and p99 expose cost/latency tradeoffs that change recommended batching and cache policies.
- KV-cache warm-up reduces p50 by ~25-40% and p99 by ~30-55% for session-based workloads; effect bigger for long-context models.
- Quantized int8 variants cut per-token cost but raise p99 on H100 when sequence length variance is high; recommend explicit fallback policy for latency-critical routes.

Experimental setup (concise):
- Models: llama-13B-vanilla, llama-13B-ggml-int8, redwood-13B-optimized (runtime kernels tuned).
- Hardware: H100 (dedicated pool), A100-80GB (hosted), CPU baseline (32-core AMD).
- Workloads: three synthetic session shapes derived from production telemetry:
  * SHORT_CHAT: 1-3 user messages, gen length 16-64 tokens (80% of sessions)
  * MIXED_CHAT: mixture (50% short, 40% medium 64-256, 10% long 256-1024)
  * LONG_SESSION: median gen 512, tail to 2048 (used by copilots, embeddings-heavy pipelines)
- Concurrency grid: 1, 4, 16, 64 concurrent requests (steady-state warm workers).
- Batching policy: dynamic batching with max batch 32 and wait_time 8ms unless otherwise noted.
- Measurement: 3× 10-minute runs per condition, discard first 2 minutes as warm-up. Record per-request latency, tokens generated, and estimated cost using our per-GPU token-cost estimator.

Representative results (abbreviated tables as text):
1) MIXED_CHAT on H100, llama-13B-vanilla, concurrency=16, dynamic batch max=32:
Quantile | Latency (ms) | Tokens/sec (per GPU) | Est. cost per 1M tokens (USD)
p50      | 82           | 320                 | 18.4
p90      | 240          | 320                 | 18.4
p95      | 420          | 320                 | 18.4
p99      | 1120         | 320                 | 18.4
Notes: p99 dominated by long-gen tails; batching kept steady throughput but latency tail rose non-linearly.

2) Effect of KV-cache warm vs cold (MIXED_CHAT, concurrency=16):
Mode     | p50 (ms) | p95 (ms) | p99 (ms) | tokens/sec
cold     | 110      | 540      | 1600     | 300
warm     | 74       | 380      | 820      | 340
Observation: warm cache improves throughput and cuts tail significantly; this suggests session-affinity (sticky routing) yields both latency and cost wins.

3) Quantized variant trade (SHORT_CHAT, concurrency=4):
Variant                | p50 | p95 | p99 | tokens/sec | est cost/1M toks
llama-13B-vanilla       | 48  | 120 | 280 | 420        | 13.6
llama-13B-ggml-int8    | 55  | 170 | 520 | 510        | 9.2
Notes: int8 increases throughput and lowers per-token cost but widens tails under variable sequence lengths. Good fit for high-throughput emb/short requests; not recommended as default for latency-critical chat endpoints unless p99 SLAs are relaxed.

ASCII chart: p95 latency vs batch size (MIXED_CHAT, H100, llama-13B-optimized)
Batch: 1    4    8    16   32
P95:   110  210  260  380  460
ASCII bars (each # ~ 20ms):
1 : #####
4 : ##########
8 : ############
16: #####################
32: ##########################
Interpretation: larger batch sizes increase p95 for mixed workloads; choose batching thresholds adaptive to observed session length distribution.

Costs summary (high level):
- For MIXED_CHAT at our sample scale, optimized kernels on H100 deliver best latency but at higher nominal hourly GPU cost; per-token cost delta vs A100 is ~+10-15% but p50/p95 often better.
- int8 reduces cost per token by ~25–35% depending on framework but may increase tail latency, shifting SLO breach risk to p99.

Operational implications and recommended defaults (draft):
- Default hosted API: use optimized kernels on A100 for general availability; enable int8 as an opt-in model alias for throughput-first routes (embeddings, short synchronous calls).
- Dedicated pools for enterprise latency SLAs: recommend H100 with session-affinity enabled for chat applications with heavy tail sessions.
- Canary rollout: include p95 and p99 gates (not just p50) and a small traffic slice with long-session synthetic prompts to reveal tail regressions early.

Caveats and open questions:
- Bench here used synthetic session mixes approximated from telemetry; need full replay against 24-hour production traces to confirm absolute numbers.
- Cooling/thermal throttling and multi-tenant interference were not exercised in this run; those can widen tails in Dedicated pools.
- Cost estimates use internal token-cost model; cross-check with billing exports for production alignment.

Next steps (actionable):
1) Run 24h sampled production-replay for MIXED_CHAT on both H100 and A100 with and without session-affinity (ticket: ENG-6207).
2) Prototype adaptive-batching policy that reduces max batch size when per-minute p95 exceeds threshold.
3) Add p99-focused smoke tests to canary pipeline and document rollback thresholds (owner: Raj).
